facts.statement: OneHotEncoder learns categories from fit data and represents each categorical value with the corresponding indicator columns.
Fit the encoder on the training categories, inspect categories_, and use transform for validation inputs without relearning the mapping.
Choose handle_unknown explicitly: its default error rejects unknown categories, whereas ignore produces all-zero indicators for an unknown category in that feature.
Missing categorical values can be represented as a learned category when present at fit time; missing values absent from the learned categories follow the unknown-category behavior.
Write assert predicate checks for the declared valid, boundary and failure cases; a false predicate raises AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution.
Build the training-category dictionary from the fitted encoder’s categories_ and feature names, and keep list-based known, unseen and missing cases aligned with that stored mapping.

practice.objective: Write the required imports and a Python function that fits OneHotEncoder on training zone rows, explicitly declares handle_unknown, and builds a training-category dictionary from categories_ under the feature name zone. Create reusable list-based known, unseen and missing fixtures, transform them without refitting, and author assertions checking their outputs against the stored mapping. Exercise both error and ignore policies, including missing values present and absent during fit.
practice.success: Known categories activate the indicator specified by the stored training mapping. Transformation preserves categories_ and output width. Unseen categories and missing values absent during fit produce all-zero indicators under ignore and raise ValueError under error. Missing values represented during fit activate their learned indicator. Learner-written assertions verify valid, boundary and failure cases.

live_code.required_skill: Implement and verify a training-fitted categorical encoder using imports, a learner-defined function, a category dictionary, reusable list fixtures and assert predicates.
live_code.starter_state_intent: Supply only illustrative zone training rows containing north and south, a second training fixture that also contains np.nan, the feature name zone, and separate reusable nested-list cases for north, east and np.nan. Leave imports, the function, dictionary construction, transformation and assertions for the learner to write.
live_code.observable_success: The function returns encoded validation rows and a zone category dictionary derived from categories_. Assertions establish indicator positions from that dictionary, unchanged fitted categories and output width, the learned missing indicator, and all-zero unknown outputs under ignore. Exception checks establish rejection under error without refitting on validation rows.
